title: Conway's Law and the Shape of Large Systems (1967/1968)
explainer: Melvin Conway's paper 'How Do Committees Invent?' (rejected by Harvard Business Review, published in Datamation in 1968) argued that a system's structure ends up mirroring the communication structure of the organization that builds it. Fred Brooks later dubbed this 'Conway's Law' in The Mythical Man-Month, and it is now a standard lens for why team topology and system architecture have to be designed together at organization scale.

title: Brooks's Law and the Mythical Man-Month (1975)
explainer: Fred Brooks, reflecting on managing IBM's OS/360 project, observed that adding people to a late software project tends to make it later, because coordination overhead grows faster than work capacity as a team scales. This is a direct, cautionary data point for anyone designing architecture meant to let large organizations divide work across many teams without drowning in communication costs.
